_comment: Risk thresholds, checked by the scanner on every run.
These do not block anything — `toreda order` places whatever you confirm.
They decide when the scanner taps you on the shoulder. Set them to where
you would ACTUALLY want warning: a threshold you intend to ignore is worse
than none, because it trains you to skim the block where real stop-loss
breaches appear.
stopLossPct      Percent from entry at which a position should be sold.
defaultMaxWeight Largest share of the portfolio one symbol may occupy.
trimProfitPct    Gain at which a position past its ceiling becomes a trim.
Overrides are deliberate, dated exceptions with a written reason. The date
and reason are the point: without them, an override is indistinguishable
from drift when you review it six months later. Example:
"overrides": {
"GOOGL": {
"maxWeight": 0.40,
"reason": "Long-term holding; accepting the concentration."
An override raises the SIZE ceiling only. The stop loss is changed per
symbol only by a stop exception, and an exception that LOOSENS the stop
must have an end date (`until`, inclusive). Conviction about a company is
not a reason to tolerate an open loss indefinitely; holding through a known
event, like earnings, is a decision with a horizon. After `until`, the
default stop and its SELL alert come back. A looser stop with no end date
does not apply. A TIGHTER stop may be open-ended (leave `until` empty).
"stopOverrides": {
"MSFT": {
"stopLossPct": -15,
"reason": "Holding through the earnings report; reassess on the results."
stopSizing       Optional. Sizes each stock's stop to how much it moves, and
measures it from the high since you bought. Off (null) by
default; stopLossPct then applies to everything, from entry.
With it on, stopLossPct is the stop for a stock with too
little history to size one. See docs/scanner.md.
"stopSizing": {
"volMultiple": 2,      stop = 2x the stock's typical two-week move,
"narrowestPct": -8,    but never tighter than this
"widestPct": -30,      or wider than this,
"trailing": true       measured from the highest close since you bought
coreSymbols      Broad funds held as the core of the account. No stop at all:
selling an index fund into a correction is the opposite of
why it is held. Example: ["VOO", "SCHD"]
